title: Envoy no longer treats private IPs as internal by default — gateways that rely on `x-envoy-*` internal headers lose them

detection.reason: whether a route depends on x-envoy internal headers is request-time behaviour; the gateway Deployments are the visible population

quote: As of Envoy 1.33, the default internalAddressConfig is set to an empty set. In previous versions the default was all private IPs. To preserve internal headers when useRemoteAddress is set or at the gateway, the internalAddressConfig must be set explicitly
remediation: Where ingress gateways depend on `x-envoy-*` headers from in-mesh callers, configure `meshNetworks` with the mesh CIDRs (gateways use it as soon as it is set); sidecars with `useRemoteAddress` additionally need `ENABLE_HCM_INTERNAL_NETWORKS=true` on istiod. Never list all private IPs — that leaves the gateway open to header manipulation (GHSA-ffhv-fvxq-r6mf). Otherwise no action.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/proxyv2"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image'  # each printed gateway stops trusting x-envoy headers from private IPs unless ENABLE_HCM_INTERNAL_NETWORKS and meshNetworks are set

title: DNS traffic honours `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutbound*` annotations (in effect since 1.23, documented at 1.25) — excluded ranges and ports no longer get DNS proxying
quote: DNS traffic (UDP and TCP) now respects pod-level traffic annotations like `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundIPRanges` and `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundPorts`.
remediation: Pods that exclude an IP range or port containing their DNS server (or port 53) stop having DNS captured by the sidecar; names that only resolved through Istio DNS proxying (ServiceEntry hosts, auto-allocated IPs) fail there. Narrow the exclusion or drop the DNS port from it. Istio's note says the change actually shipped in 1.23 and was left out of those release notes — a cluster already on 1.23/1.24 is living with it now.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations // {} | keys[] | startswith("traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutbound")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed pod's exclusions now also apply to its DNS traffic

title: Ambient workloads get DNS proxying by default — new pods only, unless iptables reconciliation is on

detection.reason: the change applies to every pod in an ambient namespace; those namespaces are the visible population

quote: DNS proxying is enabled by default for ambient workloads in this release. Note that only new pods will have DNS enabled, existing pods will not have their DNS traffic captured.
remediation: After upgrading istio-cni, pods in ambient namespaces resolve through ztunnel DNS once restarted; existing pods keep direct DNS until restarted or until `cni.ambient.reconcileIptablesOnStartup=true` reconciles them. Expect mixed behaviour until every ambient pod has cycled; opt out with `cni.ambient.dnsCapture=false`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ns -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["istio.io/dataplane-mode"] == "ambient") | .metadata.name'  # pods in each printed namespace get DNS capture once restarted after the 1.25 istio-cni upgrade

title: Istio's Grafana dashboards now need Grafana 7.2 or later

detection.reason: the Grafana version is an image tag on a Deployment the mesh does not own; the dashboards are files

quote: The changes require version 7.2 or later of Grafana.
remediation: Upgrade Grafana to 7.2+ before importing the 1.25 dashboards; older Grafana renders them incorrectly.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("grafana/grafana"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image'  # the printed image tag must be 7.2 or later for the 1.25 dashboards

title: OpenCensus tracing is removed — the legacy `meshConfig.defaultConfig.tracing.openCensusAgent` tracer stops working

detection.reason: extension providers live inside the istio ConfigMap's mesh YAML, whose keys the projection keeps and whose contents it does not

quote: Because Envoy has removed OpenCensus tracing extension, we have removed OpenCensus support from Istio. If you are using OpenCensus, you should migrate to OpenTelemetry.
remediation: What 1.25 removes is the legacy bootstrap tracer: `meshConfig.defaultConfig.tracing.openCensusAgent` (and the same setting under a pod's `proxy.istio.io/config`). Move it to an `opentelemetry` extension provider selected through the Telemetry API before upgrading proxies; spans are otherwise dropped. (The `opencensus` extension-provider path was already removed at 1.23 — see that release's rule.)
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.data.mesh != null) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .data.mesh | split("\n")[] | select(test("openCensusAgent|opencensus")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line configures the OpenCensus bootstrap tracer, which 1.25 removes

title: ztunnel chart resources are now named after the Helm release — a release not called `ztunnel` renames its DaemonSet (downtime)

detection.reason: the Helm release name is release metadata; the ztunnel DaemonSet is the object that would be renamed

quote: If you are installing the chart with a release name other than `ztunnel`, the resource names will change, triggering downtime. In this scenario, it is recommended to set `--set resourceName=ztunnel` to override back to the previous default.
remediation: If the ztunnel Helm release is not named `ztunnel`, add `--set resourceName=ztunnel` to the 1.25 upgrade so the DaemonSet keeps its name; otherwise the old DaemonSet is deleted and a new one created, interrupting ambient traffic on every node. (1.26 reverts the default.)
verifyCommand: helm list -A -o json | jq -r '.[] | select(.chart | startswith("ztunnel")) | select(.name != "ztunnel") | .namespace + "/" + .name + " " + .chart'  # a printed release is not named ztunnel and needs --set resourceName=ztunnel at 1.25

title: `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/kubevirtInterfaces` is deprecated in favour of `istio.io/reroute-virtual-interfaces` — and istio-cni 1.25–1.27 ignores the old key
remediation: Rename the annotation on the listed pod templates to `istio.io/reroute-virtual-interfaces` (same comma-separated interface list) BEFORE upgrading istio-cni: on clusters that use istio-cni for sidecar redirection, 1.25–1.27 read only the new key, so a pod carrying just the old one loses its interface rerouting (istio/istio#57662, fixed 1.28). The `istio-init` (non-CNI) path keeps honouring the old key.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations // {} | keys[] | startswith("traffic.sidecar.istio.io/kubevirtInterfaces")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed pod uses the deprecated annotation

title: `ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE` in proxyMetadata is deprecated in favour of the status-based IP auto-allocation

detection.reason: proxyMetadata is set in meshConfig or in a per-pod proxy.istio.io/config annotation; the projection keeps the annotation key and the ConfigMap keys, not their contents

quote: **Deprecated** use of `ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE` in proxyMetadata in favor of https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/traffic-management/dns-proxy/#dns-auto-allocation-v2.
remediation: Keep working installs as they are; for new ones, and before the flag is removed, rely on `PILOT_ENABLE_IP_AUTOALLOCATE` (default on at 1.25, which writes `status.addresses` on ServiceEntries) and remove `ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE` from `meshConfig.defaultConfig.proxyMetadata` and per-pod `proxy.istio.io/config` annotations.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods,cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(tojson | test("ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE")) | .kind + " " + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed object sets the deprecated proxyMetadata flag

title: IP auto-allocation v2 is on by default — ServiceEntries without `spec.addresses` gain `status.addresses`

detection.reason: applies to ServiceEntries lacking spec.addresses, an absence the projection cannot list; the entries are the visible population

quote: `ServiceEntry` objects without `spec.address` set will now see a new field, `status.addresses`, automatically set. Note these will not be used unless proxies are configured to do DNS proxying, which remains off-by-default.
remediation: No action for most meshes. Controllers or GitOps diffs that own ServiceEntry status must tolerate the new `status.addresses`; meshes with DNS proxying on should confirm the allocated addresses do not collide with the legacy `ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE` range, or set `PILOT_ENABLE_IP_AUTOALLOCATE=false` on istiod.
verifyCommand: kubectl get serviceentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.addresses == null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " status.addresses=" + ((.status.addresses // []) | length | tostring)'  # each printed ServiceEntry gets status.addresses allocated from 1.25

title: GKE gets an explicit `global.platform=gke` profile; the istio-cni chart's GKE autodetection is deprecated in its favour

detection.reason: Helm values are not collected and the node provider is not part of the DaemonSet row; the hint names the istio-cni DaemonSet and the command reads the nodes' providerID

quote: When installing on GKE, use `--set global.platform=gke` (Helm) or `--set values.global.platform=gke` (istioctl) to apply GKE-specific value overrides. This replaces the previous GKE autodetection based on K8S version used in the `istio-cni` chart.
remediation: On GKE, set `global.platform=gke` on every chart (base, istiod, istio-cni, ztunnel) so the CNI bin/conf directories, the ResourceQuota (added at 1.26) and the node-agent settings come from the profile. The 1.25–1.28 istio-cni chart still autodetects GKE from the node version string (the template calls it deprecated), so an install without the value keeps working for now; istioctl sets it automatically from 1.26, Helm never does.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.providerID}' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -c '^gce://'  # a non-zero count is a GKE cluster: set global.platform=gke on the Istio charts
